candidate.blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — use of PPE and prevention of occupational exposure
candidate.educational_objective: Explain why correct PPE donning and doffing technique and training are necessary to prevent occupational exposure and self-contamination.

options.A: PPE technique is intuitive, so formal training is unnecessary.
options.B: Incorrect donning or removal can reduce protection and cause self-contamination or exposure.
options.C: Training is needed only during a recognized outbreak.
options.D: Experienced staff do not need training in PPE use.

candidate.rationale: CDC/NIOSH guidance states that PPE must be donned properly to provide intended protection and removed in a way that avoids self-contamination. CDC occupational infection-prevention guidance also identifies proper donning, doffing, adjustment, and use of PPE as required education and training content. Therefore B is correct.
candidate.source_claim_supported: PPE must be donned correctly for intended protection and doffed to avoid self-contamination; healthcare personnel education includes how to properly don, doff, adjust and wear PPE.
candidate.source_document_title: Donning and Doffing PPE: Proper Wearing, Removal, and Disposal; Occupational Infection Prevention and Control: Education and Training
candidate.source_locator: NIOSH Module 3 — Donning and Doffing PPE; CDC Education and Training — Personal Protective Equipment standard elements
candidate.source_organization: CDC / National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health (NIOSH)
candidate.source_version_date: NIOSH reviewed Oct. 3, 2022; CDC occupational training page Apr. 12, 2024; current resources rechecked 2026
candidate.stem: Why must healthcare personnel be trained to don and remove personal protective equipment (PPE) correctly?
